title: Quasi-equivalence model structure on small dg categories
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A cochain complex is a $\mathbf Z$-graded abelian group with a degree-$1$ differential $d$ satisfying $d^2=0$; a quasi-isomorphism is a chain map inducing isomorphisms on every cohomology group. A small dg category over $\mathbf Z$ has a set of objects, cochain complexes of morphisms, and associative unital chain-map compositions. A dg functor preserves these compositions and units. A quasi-equivalence is a dg functor inducing quasi-isomorphisms on every morphism complex and an essentially surjective functor on $H^0$, the category obtained by taking degree-zero cohomology of each morphism complex. The category of small dg categories has a cofibrantly generated model structure with these weak equivalences. Its fibrations are dg functors $p$ which are degreewise surjective on morphism complexes and lift isomorphisms with specified source in $H^0$: every isomorphism $p(x)\to y$ lifts to an isomorphism $x\to x'$ with $p(x')=y$ and whose image under $H^0p$ is the given isomorphism. Here a model structure means retract-closed weak equivalences satisfying two-out-of-three and two weak factorization systems (cofibrations, trivial fibrations) and (trivial cofibrations, fibrations), with functorial factorizations; trivial means also a weak equivalence, and cofibrantly generated means these systems are generated by sets of maps. All objects are fibrant. Trivial fibrations are precisely dg functors surjective on objects and degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphisms on morphism complexes. Thus a cofibrant object is exactly one whose map from the empty category has the left lifting property against those trivial fibrations.

There is a functorial trivial fibration $q_{\mathcal A}:Q\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ with cofibrant source and the identity map on object sets. For any cofibrant dg category $\mathcal A$, each complex $\mathcal A(x,y)$ is cofibrant for the projective model structure on unbounded complexes of abelian groups (fibrations are degreewise surjections, weak equivalences are quasi-isomorphisms); in particular it is homotopically flat, meaning its tensor product with any quasi-isomorphism is a quasi-isomorphism. In this dg-category model structure, morphisms from a cofibrant object to any object in the localization at quasi-equivalences are represented by strict dg functors, modulo model-category homotopy (the equivalence relation generated by maps from cylinder objects, where a cylinder of $X$ factors its fold $X\amalg X\to X$ as a cofibration followed by a weak equivalence). Enlarging the universes preserves morphism sets and mapping spaces between the original small dg categories.
